title: Finite normal model over a finite part of a perfect closure
statement: Let k and K be fields [def-weil-field], with K/k a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] which is perfect and purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and let q:X to Spec k be a finite type morphism [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There is a finite intermediate field E of K/k, a scheme Y with a finite surjective morphism f:Y to X_E [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and a dense open U of X_E such that f inverse U is dense in Y and f restricted to U is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Every stalk of Y_K is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Here Y_K is the base change of f followed by the projection X_E to Spec E along E to K. This asserts a finite model with a dense closed-immersion locus, without identifying it with normalization at the finite stage or asserting normality over every field extension of E.

source.place: Tag 0BXT, proof through the descent of the dense open and its closed immersion; Limits Tags 01ZM, 01ZO, 01Z4, 01ZP

proof.text: Use the given perfect purely inseparable overfield $K/k$. Index its finite intermediate extensions by inclusion. This is a nonempty directed set with union $K$: a finite family $a_1,\ldots,a_m$ lies in $k(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$, which is finite because each $a_j$ satisfies $T^{q^{n_j}}-a_j^{q^{n_j}}$ over $k$; the compositum of two such fields is generated by their two finite generating families. Every intermediate field is purely inseparable by the same power condition. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the inverse limit of their spectra. The same assertion for $X_K=\varprojlim X_{k_i}$ follows on every affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ from $A\otimes_kK=\varinjlim(A\otimes_kk_i)$; tensor generators and their bilinear relations give this colimit identity. Transition maps are affine since on these charts they are maps of spectra.

For each field $F$ occurring here, $X_F$ and its reduction are finite type over $F$: affine charts are generated by the images of the finitely many generators of the original chart, and taking the quotient by the nilradical preserves these generators. Fields are Noetherian (their ideals are $0$ and $1$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives Noetherianity, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] gives quasi-separatedness. Normalize $(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ componentwise and call the result $N_K$. The finite surjective map supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change], followed by reduction, is a finite surjective map $\nu_K:N_K\to X_K$: on an affine chart the reduction map is $A\to A/\sqrt0$, and a finite module over this quotient is also a finite module over $A$.

The normalization of each integral component has domain stalks, and its stalks are integrally closed by Scheme.Hom.isIntegrallyClosed_stalk_normalization applied to its function-field spectrum. Finite coproducts have the same stalk properties because coprojections are open immersions. The finite morphism to the Noetherian target is finitely presented: it is locally of finite type, and finite type algebras over Noetherian rings are finitely presented.

Apply the existing theorem Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation to the finite-presentation normalization map over the limit X_K. This directly gives a finite-presentation model Y_i over X_i and a Cartesian comparison. No new gluing datum is required: the already proved theorem performs that construction. The source and stages are qcqs by Noetherianity and finite presentation.

Apply the finiteness descent theorem to this model, viewed as a morphism over the initial stage of the tail system. Enlarge the finite intermediate field to make the model map finite. Base change to K is still the original componentwise normalization, hence has normal domain stalks. No normality over the finite stage, and no geometric normality conclusion, is needed in this lemma.

By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change], the normal locus of $(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is dense open and the normalization is an isomorphism over it. Let $V_K$ be the corresponding open of $X_K$, using the identical underlying space of reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Then $\nu_K^{-1}(V_K)\to V_K$ is a closed immersion with source $(V_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Its preimage is dense in $N_K$: each component normalization has the same function field as its reduced integral component by [def-sc-normalization], so its generic point lies above the generic point of that component, which belongs to the normal locus. Every component therefore meets the preimage. All these opens are quasi-compact, since the schemes are Noetherian by step 2 (for $N_K$ use its finite type over $K$, immediate from its finite map).

source.place: Tag 0BXT dense-open paragraph; Varieties Tag 0BXR and Morphisms Tag 035O

proof.text: Use [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] on the system $X_{k_j}$ to descend $V_K$ to a quasi-compact open $V\subset X_{k_i}$ after another enlargement. For closed-immersion descent take the tail system $S_j=\operatorname{Spec}k_j$ with limit $\operatorname{Spec}K$; the two schemes over its initial stage are $\nu^{-1}(V)$ and $V$. Restrict the descended finite map to $\nu^{-1}(V)\to V$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion]. Its base change to $K$ is the closed immersion in step 6, it is locally of finite type (finite), and its source and target are qcqs: $Y$ is finite type over $k_i$, hence Noetherian, and inverse images of quasi-compact opens under the finite affine map are quasi-compact; they are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Enlarge once more to obtain a closed immersion on this open. The descended open is in $X_{k_i}$, correcting the source's typo $V\subset Y$.

source.place: Tag 0BXT open/closed-immersion descent paragraph (correct V subset X_{k_i}); Limits Tags 01Z4 and 01ZP

proof.text: At the last stage E, the base-change projections X_K to X_E and Y_K to Y are homeomorphisms, since K/E is purely inseparable. The Cartesian comparison identifies the finite model after K-base change with the original normalization map. Thus its surjectivity reflects to Y to X_E. The descended target open U has preimage the original dense open, and its inverse image in Y has preimage the dense normalization open. Homeomorphisms identify closures, so both are dense. The descended restricted map is a closed immersion. E/k is finite by the indexing construction. Empty schemes use the empty normalization and empty open and cause no exception.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_perfectClosure_finite_normal_model
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    [IsPurelyInseparable k K] [PerfectField K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (q : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType q] [QuasiCompact q] :
    ∃ E : IntermediateField k K, Module.Finite k E ∧
      ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u})
        (f : Y ⟶ pullback q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E))))
        (U : (pullback q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E)))).Opens),
        IsFinite f ∧ Surjective f ∧
        Dense (Set.range U.ι) ∧
        Dense (f ⁻¹ᵁ U : Set Y) ∧ IsClosedImmersion (f ∣_ U) ∧
        ∀ z : (pullback
            (f ≫ pullback.snd q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E))))
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap E K))) : Scheme.{u}),
          IsDomain ((pullback
            (f ≫ pullback.snd q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E))))
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap E K)))).presheaf.stalk z) ∧
          IsIntegrallyClosed ((pullback
            (f ≫ pullback.snd q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E))))
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap E K)))).presheaf.stalk z)
